newsitem.title: UK: Manufacturing orders up in most UK regions - CBI.
newsitem.headline: Manufacturing orders up in most UK regions - CBI.

text.p: Orders for manufactured goods rose in eight out of the 11 UK regions in the four months to October, with Wales, Northern Ireland, East Anglia and Scotland seeing the greatest increase, a business survey said on Friday.

The quarterly Regional Trends survey of the Confederation of British Industry (CBI) and consultancy Business Strategies said even in regions where orders fell -- the South West, Yorkshire & Humberside and the East Midlands -- the fall was only modest.
Export demand over the past four months was strongest in Northern Ireland. "In the UK as a whole, the growth in domestic orders was faster than that for export orders," the survey said.
Firms in every region expect orders to increase over the next four months, although in the North only a slight increase is foreseen.
"Firms in Wales and East Anglia expect the largest rises in total orders, and firms in the South West, Wales and Northern Ireland expect the largest rises in export orders," the survey said.
Manufacturers in all regions except the North expect output to rise over the coming months.
Unit wage costs fell over the past four months in seven regions but rose in Northern Ireland, East Anglia the North West and the North.
Firms' domestic prices fell in eight regions, rising only Northern Ireland, the East Midlands and the North West.

Over the next four months, domestic prices are expected to rise in six regions and fall in five. "Only firms in the East Midlands, the North West and Yorkshire & Humberside expect the rises in domestic prices to be more than trivial," the survey said.
Business confidence has increased in eight regions with East Anglia and Scotland the most optimistic.
"Only firms in the North and Northern Ireland reported a fall in confidence," the survey said.
The survey covered 1,155 manufacturing firms and was carried out between September 20 and October 9.
